case_title: Manikandan v. State by the Inspector of Police
neutral_facts: The prosecution case alleged that the deceased, who was staying with his parents, instructed the accused no.1 to deliver idlis at his home. On the evening of the incident, the deceased came home and asked his mother if the accused had delivered the idlis. Upon learning that the accused had not, the deceased went to the accused's house, where a commotion occurred due to an altercation. The deceased's mother and brother-in-law arrived at the scene. The accused no.1 entered his house, retrieved a billhook, and assaulted the deceased with it. The deceased ran to a nearby garden, where the accused no.1 and accused no.2 chased him. Accused no.2 held the deceased while accused no.1 inflicted a fatal blow with the billhook. The deceased's mother and other relatives arrived and witnessed the incident. The prosecution relied on the testimony of the deceased's family members and other witnesses to establish the sequence of events.
